strings.name: Raj Subramaniam
strings.role: President and CEO of FedEx Corporation
strings.country: Originally from India; career mainly in the United States
strings.summary: Raj Subramaniam joined FedEx in 1991, held marketing and operations leadership roles, and became group CEO in 2022. Under his leadership, the group pursued express business integration and completed the Freight spin-off and Supply Chain subsidiary sale in 2026; the long-term effects of restructuring remain to be seen.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through 17 November 2026. Birth date is omitted because sources conflict. Distinguish the group from operating companies, legal merger from network integration, and the Freight spin-off from the Supply Chain sale; forecasts are not results.
strings.influence.rationale: Leads FedEx and advances operational integration, contributing to international logistics and supply-chain services.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Bachelor’s in chemical engineering from IIT, master’s in chemical engineering from Syracuse University, and MBA from the University of Texas at Austin.
strings.facts.f2.label: Scope of roles
strings.facts.f2.value: Became group President and COO in March 2019 and CEO on 1 June 2022; being a director does not mean being board chairman.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Advancing express business integration
strings.highlights.h1.text: Ground and Services merged into Federal Express in 2024; the legal merger does not mean all network synergies have been achieved.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Reshaping the business portfolio
strings.highlights.h2.text: The Freight spin-off and Supply Chain subsidiary sale were completed separately in 2026, involving different businesses and transaction structures.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Comments on quarterly operations
strings.timeline.t1.text: The earnings release quoted his comments on network and cost management; he signed a CEO certification the same day.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Sale of Supply Chain subsidiary
strings.timeline.t2.text: The group completed the sale of FedEx Supply Chain to CMA CGM; this was not a sale of all of FedEx.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Completion of Freight spin-off
strings.timeline.t3.text: The group distributed 80.1% of Freight shares to shareholders and retained 19.9% at separation, creating an independent listed company.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Operating-company merger
strings.timeline.t4.text: Ground and Services merged into Federal Express; he also became the latter’s President and CEO from that date.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Becoming group CEO
strings.timeline.t5.text: Succeeded founder Frederick W. Smith; the March succession announcement is not treated as the effective start date.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becoming group President and COO
strings.timeline.t6.text: Moved from operating-company leadership to a group role, before becoming group CEO.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Leading group marketing and communications
strings.timeline.t7.text: Served as Executive Vice President and Chief Marketing and Communications Officer until December 2018.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joining FedEx
strings.timeline.t8.text: Began analytical and management work at Federal Express, later taking on responsibilities across regions.
